about: Anatomy & Physiology concept dependency map (Phase 0 of docs/anp-spec.md). Topics are listed in course order; every concept names the topic that teaches it and the concepts it directly depends on. A concept’s aliases are the words its topic owns (for the glossary and the page check), not strict synonyms; a parenthetical marks a display label that the page check skips because the bare word has two meanings. A dependency may only point at a concept taught in the same or an earlier topic, unless the topic lists it under previews. fullIn marks a short pulled-forward version whose full treatment comes later. enrichment marks a concept beyond the three coverage standards (OpenStax 2e, TEAS 7, HAPS), kept for the nursing and EMT audience. Open questions and contested science live in docs/anp-needs-author.md. Checked by scripts/check-anp-map.mjs.

coreConcepts.name: Homeostasis
coreConcepts.summary: Sensors, a control center and effectors hold a regulated variable near a set point, mostly by negative feedback.

coreConcepts.name: Flow down gradients
coreConcepts.summary: Blood, air, ions, water and heat all move from high to low pressure, concentration, voltage or temperature, at a rate set by the gradient and the resistance.

coreConcepts.name: Cell-to-cell communication
coreConcepts.summary: Cells coordinate through electrical signals, chemical messengers and direct connections; a signal only acts on cells that carry its receptor.

coreConcepts.name: Structure and function
coreConcepts.summary: What a structure can do follows from its shape and parts, from molecules to whole organs.

coreConcepts.name: Mass balance
coreConcepts.summary: The amount of any substance in the body changes only by what enters, leaves, is made or is used up.

coreConcepts.name: Energy and ATP
coreConcepts.summary: Cells capture energy from food as ATP and spend it on pumping, moving and building.

coreConcepts.name: Membranes and compartments
coreConcepts.summary: Membranes divide the body into compartments with different contents, and control what crosses between them.

coreConcepts.name: Interdependence of systems
coreConcepts.summary: No system works alone: a change in one system is sensed and answered by others.

circularDependencies.problem: Muscle contraction (A&P I muscle chapter) needs action potentials, but the nervous system chapters come after muscle. The heart also needs them.
circularDependencies.detail: Short foundation topics on the resting potential and on graded vs action potentials. Muscle, neurons and the heart all build on them.

circularDependencies.problem: Bone (calcium, growth), skin (vitamin D) and the neuromuscular junction need hormones, receptors and neurotransmitters before the endocrine and synapse chapters.
circularDependencies.detail: Ligands, receptor proteins, target cells, hormones vs neurotransmitters, second messengers and intracellular receptors at a basic level.

circularDependencies.problem: Every system chapter uses the stimulus to response loop.
circularDependencies.detail: Homeostasis and feedback loops closes Foundations, after nerves, action potentials, hormones and glands are taught, so the loop's pathways need no preview boxes. A one-line definition of homeostasis and normal range sits in the first topic so pages 1 to 32 can use the word. Its two standard examples still need previews: the hypothalamus (body temperature) and oxytocin (childbirth).

circularDependencies.problem: Diffusion, osmosis, pressure-driven flow and resistance are used by cells, capillaries, lungs and kidneys.
circularDependencies.detail: The flow equation F = ΔP/R and the radius effect are taught once, generally, and every system reuses them.

circularDependencies.problem: Muscle energy systems (A&P I) need glycolysis, anaerobic metabolism and aerobic respiration; the metabolism chapter is in A&P II. Breathing also needs CO2 as a metabolic waste.
circularDependencies.detail: An overview of glycolysis, aerobic respiration and metabolic CO2, without the enzyme-by-enzyme detail.

circularDependencies.problem: Skin thermoregulation, the ANS chapter and inflammation all need vasoconstriction and vasodilation before the vessels chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: Taught with smooth muscle: smooth muscle in a vessel wall changes its radius, and the radius sets resistance (already known from the primer).

circularDependencies.problem: Arteries, veins and capillaries are named in epithelium (endothelium), skin, bone, the blood-brain barrier and the ANS long before the cardiovascular chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: A one-paragraph basic definition inside the organ system overview: arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins toward it, capillaries are where exchange happens.

circularDependencies.problem: Tissue repair, wound healing, burns and fracture repair need inflammation before the immune chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: The four signs and the basic mechanism (damaged tissue releases chemicals that dilate vessels and make them leaky).

circularDependencies.problem: Connective tissue, red cell recycling, alveoli and inflammation mention macrophages before innate immunity.
circularDependencies.detail: Macrophage as a resident phagocytic cell of connective tissue.

circularDependencies.problem: The bone chapter names red marrow as the site of blood cell formation; the blood chapter comes much later.
circularDependencies.detail: Basic definition in the bone chapter; the blood chapter teaches stem cell lineages.

circularDependencies.problem: Lymphocytes and blood typing need antigens and antibodies; the immune chapter follows the blood chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: Used in two blood topics, so it gets a short taught version instead of two preview boxes.

circularDependencies.problem: Long-term blood pressure control (cardiovascular) needs renin, angiotensin and aldosterone; the urinary chapter comes after cardiovascular.
circularDependencies.detail: RAAS is taught as the control of aldosterone in the endocrine chapter. The juxtaglomerular apparatus (where renin is made) gets its anatomy in the nephron topic. Its trigger is taught as falling blood pressure, from the basic blood pressure concept in the primer.

circularDependencies.problem: The muscle tissue chapter compares cardiac to skeletal and smooth muscle before the heart chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: Intercalated discs, gap junctions and the fact that some cardiac cells set their own rhythm; the ionic mechanism waits for the heart chapter.

circularDependencies.problem: Insulin and glucagon need glycogenesis, glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis before the metabolism chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: Named and defined in one line each; the pathways come later.

circularDependencies.problem: Ketoacidosis, hyperventilation and CO2 transport all use acidosis and alkalosis before the acid-base chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: Definitions only (blood pH below or above 7.35 to 7.45).

circularDependencies.problem: The neuromuscular junction is a synapse, taught in the muscle chapter before the synapse topic.
circularDependencies.detail: A short synapse concept (synapse, synaptic cleft, pre- and postsynaptic) is taught with neurotransmitters, so the NMJ can use the words; the synapse topic generalizes from the NMJ.

circularDependencies.problem: The baroreceptor reflex needs the carotid sinus and aortic arch.
circularDependencies.detail: Inside the cardiovascular chapter, vessel structure and the named arteries and veins come before blood pressure, cardiac output and its control.

circularDependencies.problem: Fetal circulation (OpenStax puts it in the vessels chapter) needs the placenta and umbilical vessels, which are taught in development.
circularDependencies.detail: Moved to the development chapter (fetal-development-circulation). The heart chapter uses a preview box for the fossa ovalis.

circularDependencies.problem: ADH release is triggered by osmoreceptors, and the osmolarity loop is fully taught in the fluid chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: Osmoreceptors are taught with ADH in the pituitary topic; the fluid chapter completes the loop with thirst and the collecting duct.

circularDependencies.problem: Foundation pages (the organ system overview, quadrants, serous membranes, and the 'where found' lists for every epithelium and cartilage) name organs and structures whose own topics come much later.
circularDependencies.detail: The organ overview owns plain organ names (thymus, spleen, gallbladder, ureter, pleura, pericardium and so on). The tissue topics own the sites they cite as examples (epidermis, alveoli, intervertebral disc, menisci). The later topics own the detailed structure, under qualified names.

circularDependencies.problem: Tonicity (red cells in solutions), connective tissue (blood), hematopoiesis in bone and the clotting example of positive feedback all need red cells, white cells, platelets and clots long before the blood chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: One-line definitions of the three formed elements, and of a clot.

circularDependencies.problem: Pressure examples in the primer, vasoconstriction, sympathetic effects, RAAS, ANP and burn fluid loss all use blood pressure and blood volume before the cardiovascular chapter.
circularDependencies.detail: Blood pressure as the pressure blood exerts on vessel walls, in mm Hg, and blood volume as the amount of blood; systolic, diastolic and MAP wait for the cardiovascular chapter.

circularDependencies.problem: Why blood pH must stay in range is protein shape and enzyme activity, which the primer taught after pH.
circularDependencies.detail: Acids, bases, pH and buffers now follows biomolecules and enzymes. Organelles and cell junctions now come before transport, because endocytosis and exocytosis need lysosomes and the Golgi.

circularDependencies.problem: Inflammation needs chemical messengers (histamine, paracrine signaling).
circularDependencies.detail: Body membranes and tissue repair moved after chemical messengers and glands; the basic inflammation concept owns histamine and mast cells.

circularDependencies.problem: Cortisol raises blood glucose by gluconeogenesis, defined in the pancreas topic.
circularDependencies.detail: The pancreas and blood glucose now comes before the adrenal glands.

circularDependencies.problem: Hyperkalemia and hypokalemia are used by the resting potential and the heart long before electrolyte balance.
circularDependencies.detail: How blood potassium shifts the resting potential.

circularDependencies.problem: EPO release and erythropoiesis are triggered by hypoxia, taught in oxygen transport.
circularDependencies.detail: Hypoxia as too little oxygen reaching tissues.
